subject: estimating mean abundance across all sites for a ZIP pcount model?

messages.author: 1a8f87740ecf4653
messages.subject: estimating mean abundance across all sites for a ZIP pcount model?
parts:
Hi all,

I have read a number of older threads about ways to calculate mean lambda (abundance) across all sites (i.e., corrected for psi, the zero inflation factor) for a closed N-mixture model (pcount). There are a mix of comments, but it looks like Richard Chandler wrote "I need to fix predict for the ZIP model. Currently it is ignoring the zero-inflation. This was an oversight when I added the new distribution." back in 2012. 

I have a top model for estimating abundance of a sparrow species across >2000 sites, and it's based on a ZIP distribution. Mean abundance is not particularly important to me, as I already have predictions based on my predictors variables, and made all my plots. However, this mean value is something that others really seem to want on paper. I know that mean N = lambda(1-psi) for the ZIP, but I'm a bit confused about what scale psi is on in the model output. I would love to just calculate mean abundance across all sites AND confidence intervals in a simple line of code. Has this function been added/fixed in unmarked since 2012? I have all the other results and plots I need, so I'm hoping to avoid tackling any more arduous coding feats.

Thanks in advance!
Mark

Hi Mark

the scale of psi should be logit, so you have to plogis() it to get at the probability scale. About the other question, I am not sure. But here is a blurb from the AHM1 book which should be helpful.

Best regards  --- Marc



(2) Function predictSE in package AICcmodavg produces point predictions and SEs, but currently no CIs, for ZIP mixtures and allows specification of an overdispersion correction c-hat, which is used to inflate the SEs. Only predictions of  are currently available and only on the response, but not the link scale.

 

# Predictions for lambda only, incl. SE and CIs, with overdispersion

predictSE(fm5ZIP, newdata=lamNewData, print.matrix = TRUE, type="response", parm.type = "lambda", c.hat = 2.47)

 

(3) Function modavgPred in AICcmodavg can be tricked into producing point predictions with SEs and 95% CIs by providing a candidate list with a single model only. As of May 2015 no CIs are available, though for some cases 95% CIs can be obtained by adding/subtracting twice the SEs from the point estimates on the link scale and then applying the inverse link transformation.

 

# Predictions for lambda and p, incl. SE and with overdispersion, but no CIs

# Poisson model, for natural and for link scale of both lambda and p

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type = "response", c.hat = 3.82)

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type = "link", c.hat = 3.82)    # Could be used to get 95% CIs

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5), newdata=pNewData, parm.type = "detect", type = "response", c.hat = 3.82)

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5), newdata=pNewData, parm.type = "detect", type = "link", c.hat = 3.82)      # Could be used to get 95% CIs

 

# NegBin model, for natural and for link scale of both lambda and p

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5NB), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type = "response", c.hat = 1.79)

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5NB), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type = "link", c.hat = 1.79)    # Could be used to get 95% CIs

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5NB), newdata=pNewData, parm.type = "detect", type = "response", c.hat = 1.79)

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5NB), newdata=pNewData, parm.type = "detect", type = "link", c.hat = 1.79)         # Could be used to get 95% CIs

 

# ZIP model, for natural and for link scale of both lambda and p

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5ZIP), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type = "response", c.hat = 2.47)

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5ZIP), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type = "link", c.hat = 2.47)     # Not yet implemented (May 2015)

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5ZIP), newdata=pNewData, parm.type = "detect", type = "response", c.hat = 2.47)

modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5ZIP), newdata=pNewData, parm.type = "detect", type = "link", c.hat = 2.47)         # this works, so we could get 95% CIs
